traps: Nerve (axons, outside central nervous system) vs tract (axons, inside central nervous system).
Ganglion (cell bodies outside) vs nucleus (cell bodies inside); 'basal ganglia' is really a nucleus.
Spinal cord gray matter central vs brain gray matter peripheral: inverted organization.
Dorsal root ganglion only: there is NO ventral root ganglion.
Cervical nerves exit CRANIAL to their vertebra; thoracic/lumbar exit CAUDAL.
First cervical nerve: LATERAL vertebral foramen, not transverse foramen, not intervertebral foramen.
Upper motor neuron (stays in central nervous system) controls lower motor neuron (leaves it).
General visceral efferent = two-neuron chain; general somatic efferent and special visceral efferent = one neuron.
Special visceral EFFERENT = pharyngeal arch skeletal muscle; special visceral AFFERENT = taste and smell.
Dorsal BRANCH (spinal nerve, epaxial) vs dorsal ROOT (sensory, enters cord) vs dorsal HORN.
flags: Muscle spindle innervation: transcript says intrafusal fibers = beta motor neurons, gamma = 'both' (garbled). Standard anatomy (outside source): gamma = intrafusal, beta = both. Confirm before carding; only 'alpha = extrafusal, most common' is safe.

Pseudounipolar/special visceral afferent: slide says special visceral afferent = bipolar AND pseudounipolar; transcript lumps special somatic and special visceral afferent as 'essentially bipolar'. Use slide.

Nerve supporting cells: slide lists Schwann cells and fibroblasts; transcript adds satellite cells. Not contradictory, but satellite cells are spoken only (and are standardly ganglion cells, not nerve).
Lateral horn: slide shows lateral horn generically; transcript says distinct in thoracolumbar, faint in sacral segments.
Blueprint objective 'relate spinal cord segments to vertebral levels': lecture only covered spinal nerve exit relative to vertebrae, not cord segment/vertebra mismatch.
Patellar reflex: transcript garbles the effector ('border-cips') and movement; quadriceps/stifle extension inferred from slide figure and standard anatomy.
